title: Core
description: The native types and relations every workspace has.

types.title: Person
types.description: A human being.

role.description: What they do, in a few words.

types.title: Company
types.description: An organisation: a business, client, vendor or institution.

types.title: Agent
types.description: A non-human actor with its own identity, such as an AI agent or an automation.

kind.description: What sort of agent, e.g. claude-code.

types.title: Goal
types.description: An outcome that projects and tasks serve.

measure.description: How you will know it is achieved.

types.title: Area
types.description: An ongoing responsibility with no end date.

types.title: Project
types.description: A body of work with an end.

hub_at.description: How many open things an item in this project holds before it is a hub: an item with views of its own, owed them when it has none. 12 when not set. While a project is being shaped, set 1: nearly everything in it is then a hub.

recheck_days.description: How often, in days, an agent re-checks this project's oldest open items against its repository. Weekly when not set; 0 turns it off.

rechecked_at.description: When an agent last re-checked this project's oldest items.

types.title: Task
types.description: A piece of work someone can do. A commitment is a task with an owed_to relation.

recurrence.description: How often it repeats, in plain words or an RRULE.

tokens_estimated.description: How many tokens an agent expects this to take: input and output, not counting cached re-reads. Whoever plans it or picks it up says; it can be corrected.

tokens_used.description: Tokens spent on it so far, measured from the sessions that worked on it.

types.title: Experiment
types.description: A task that tests a hypothesis and produces a result.

types.title: Decision
types.description: Something decided, or still open, with its reasoning. The title is the question.

options.description: The choices being weighed, as a list of short strings, e.g. ["Hosted API", "Local model"].

types.title: Issue
types.description: A problem or risk observed, separate from the work to fix it.

tokens_estimated.description: How many tokens an agent expects fixing this to take: input and output, not counting cached re-reads. Whoever plans it or picks it up says; it can be corrected.

tokens_used.description: Tokens spent on it so far, measured from the sessions that worked on it.

types.title: Hypothesis
types.description: A belief about the world that could be wrong. The title is the statement.

types.title: Result
types.description: A recorded outcome with its evidence: a measurement, a test run, a reply.

evidence.description: Where the proof is: a path, URL or commit.

types.title: Event
types.description: Something that happens at a time: a deadline, a launch, an appointment.

types.title: Meeting
types.description: An event with participants (use the involves relation).

types.title: Resource
types.description: Something limited or exclusive that work needs: a machine, a licence, a budget, a live app.

exclusive.description: If true, only one holder at a time; everything else that needs it is blocked.

types.title: Cost
types.description: Something paid for regularly: hosting, a subscription, a licence, a domain. What agents spend per token is not kept here: it is measured from their runs.

amount.description: What is paid each time, in the currency below. Left out when nobody has said: it is then shown as not priced.

since.description: The first day it was paid for. Left out: the day it was written down.

until.description: The last day it is paid for, when that is known.

url.description: Where the bill or the plan can be looked at.

types.title: Procedure
types.description: How something is done: a checklist, playbook or rule. One a machine can run is a function.

entrypoint.description: For executable procedures: the command, skill or script.

types.title: File
types.description: A document or artefact that lives somewhere.

types.title: Idea
types.description: Something we could do.

types.title: Note
types.description: Free-form knowledge that does not fit another type.

types.title: Document
types.description: Writing for a reader, made of the map: its note is the text, and a line holding only an item's id brings that item in at that place, as a section with its title and note. Read whole with the document tool; the owner can give someone a link to it.

for.description: Who it is written for, e.g. "Sam at Northwind".

types.title: Lens
types.description: What is in a picture of the map. About a project or item, it is a view of that thing, named by its title: an item's page shows its views as a switch and opens on the first (place). About nothing, it is the workspace's: a view that can be chosen for any picture, and the one the whole map opens on. A field left empty is the built-in one. Read by the lens view.

place.description: Its order among the views of the item it is about: the lowest is the one the page opens on.

from.description: The id of the item this view starts from, when that is not the item it is about. Such a view is a shortcut: the page shows it as a way to that item.

controls.description: What the person looking may change on the page, as a list of: lit (what stays lit), far (how many steps down), closed (whether what is finished shows). Only lit when not set.

kinds.description: Types to keep, as a list: a type (flavours included) or "work"; with a leading "-", to leave out.

by.description: The kind of link that says what is inside what, e.g. part_of.

over.description: The kinds of link sent along as links, as a list, or "all".

far.description: How many steps down from the start.

lanes.description: What each item is filed under.

order.description: The number field that orders things beside each other.

fold.description: What is left out, as a list of: closed, system, unlinked.

types.title: Style
types.description: How a picture of the map is drawn. About a project or item, it is how that thing's picture looks; about nothing, the workspace's. A field left empty comes from the level above. Read only by the page that draws.

shape.description: One of the drawings that come built in, used when the style has no code of its own. nest: circles in circles, opened by zooming. boxes: titled boxes in boxes, each thing one line.

lit.description: What stays lit as it opens.

open.description: How many levels are open as it first draws.

show.description: What a thing says beside its name, as a list of: count, blocked, you, sessions, status, type, bar.

leaf.description: How a thing with nothing inside it is drawn in boxes.

column.description: The least width of a box, in pixels.

text.description: The size of names, in pixels.

radius.description: How round corners are, in pixels.

gap.description: The room between things, in pixels.

lines.description: Whether links are drawn as lines.

colors.description: Colours by name, each a hex colour: sea, land, inner, line, text, muted, blocked, you, session, done.

code.description: The drawing itself, as a JavaScript module: export default function draw({ canvas, answer, style, theme, size, tree, three, on, open, tip, cursor }). It runs in the browser of whoever looks, in a worker inside a sandboxed frame: it has a canvas to draw on and no page, no network and no storage. Written by an agent, it waits for the human to approve it before it runs. canvas is an OffscreenCanvas (2D or WebGL); answer is what the lens view answered; style is this style's other fields; theme is the page's colours (sea, land, inner, line, text, muted, blocked, you, session, done) and dark; size is { width, height, dpr }, kept current; tree() gives the answer as a tree ({ root, byId, me }, each thing with kids, up, depth and its counts all, work, blk, you, at); three() resolves to three.js; on(name, fn) hears pointerdown, pointermove, pointerup, pointerleave, wheel (each { x, y, button, buttons, deltaY, shift, ctrl }) and resize; open(id) opens an item's page; tip(text, x, y) shows words by the pointer (null hides them); cursor(name) sets the pointer. With code, shape is not used.

relations.title: depends on
relations.description: The source cannot finish until the target is closed. Drives the blockers view.

relations.title: waits on
relations.description: The source cannot move until this person, company or agent has answered or acted. Say what is awaited in the relation's props.for. Drives the blockers view; remove the link once they have.

relations.title: goes ahead without
relations.description: The event was planned with this in sight and does not wait for it: it can follow. What the event does wait for is depends_on. Drives the gate view.

relations.title: is part of
relations.description: Hierarchy: a task in a project, a project in an area.

relations.title: serves
relations.description: Why the work exists.

relations.title: is owed to
relations.description: Makes a task a commitment to someone.

relations.title: was requested by
relations.description: Who asked for it.

relations.title: involves
relations.description: Participants and stakeholders.

relations.title: works at
relations.description: Put the job title in the relation's props.role.

relations.title: is about
relations.description: A note, file, decision or issue concerns the target.

relations.title: needs
relations.description: The work cannot run without this resource. Drives the blockers view.

relations.title: holds
relations.description: Current occupancy of a resource. Created by claim, ended by release.

relations.title: tests
relations.description: The work that will settle the hypothesis.

relations.title: supports
relations.description: Evidence for.

relations.title: refutes
relations.description: Evidence against.

relations.title: assumes
relations.description: The source only makes sense if the hypothesis holds. Flagged at risk when it is refuted.

relations.title: would explain
relations.description: A suspected cause.

relations.title: addresses
relations.description: Work meant to fix or reduce the issue.

relations.title: produced
relations.description: The work led to this result, file or decision.

relations.title: is based on
relations.description: A decision or plan rests on this result or source.

relations.title: is governed by
relations.description: The rule or procedure that applies.

relations.title: supersedes
relations.description: Replaces an older version.

relations.title: relates to
relations.description: A loose link. Prefer a specific relation when one fits.
